briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 13, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Threats and Global Warnings
sections.content: Globally, climate threats are intensifying, endangering human lives in various forms. In Nepal, 21 glacial lakes have been identified as ticking time bombs for catastrophic floods, underscoring the need for a global coordinated response [9]. In the United States, bears descending into residential areas in search of food due to climate change are becoming an issue [7], and in Bolivia, fluctuating rice yields demonstrate the direct impact of climate change on agricultural productivity [3]. Furthermore, ancient trees on UK estates are suffering damage due to climate change [67], and the landscape of apple orchards worldwide is being reshaped [66], indicating widespread threats across ecosystems and agriculture. In France, a significant number of last summer's record-breaking wildfires are suspected to be intentional arson [77], and a Stanford study warns that water bills could double by 2050 due to climate change [68], posing direct threats to human life and the economy.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Technological Innovation
sections.content: The Republic of Korea is making multifaceted efforts to respond to the climate crisis and transition to a carbon-neutral society. Lotte and KAIST have completed an R&D center for climate change and carbon neutrality research, accelerating the development of core technologies in areas such as biotechnology and advanced food [1, 13, 23, 30, 35, 42, 43, 45]. The Korea Institute of Climate Change Research and the Korea CCUS Association have also agreed to collaborate on joint research for carbon neutrality [5, 6]. The role of local governments is also prominent: Gwangju Buk-gu was selected as an excellent carbon-neutral local government and received a ministerial award [15, 18, 20, 24, 26, 27, 32, 33, 37]. Changwon Special City also gained attention by demonstrating the excellence of its 'Changwon-type Carbon Neutrality Model' [14, 46]. Activities encouraging citizen participation, such as Gangwon Province's 'Net-Zero Action Group' [8], Cheonan City's 'Visiting Carbon Neutrality Classroom' [16, 36], and Gyeongju's 'Training of Citizen Environmental Experts' [19, 22], are actively underway. The South Chungcheong Provincial Council is establishing a policy foundation by forming a 'Special Committee for Just Transition' to implement carbon neutrality [29].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating the Transition to Renewable Energy and Green Hydrogen
sections.content: The expansion of renewable energy and the production of green hydrogen are emerging as key drivers for achieving carbon neutrality goals. The government is accelerating the clean energy transition by promoting 50-100MW-class green hydrogen production demonstrations, particularly in renewable energy-dense areas [48, 54]. Efforts to expand renewable energy supply are also continuing at the local government level, with Daejeon Dong-gu securing 1.2 billion KRW in national funding by achieving an 'A grade' in the Renewable Energy Convergence Support Project [49, 51, 52, 56]. In the industrial sector, HD Hyundai Electric aims to achieve RE100 by 2040 through solar power and PPAs [58]. LS Electric is pursuing joint renewable energy development cooperation with Korea Midland Power [55], demonstrating the strong commitment of companies to transition to renewable energy. Concurrently, in Jeju, methods for clean hydrogen production using renewable energy and expanding international cooperation are being explored [57]. Policy efforts to expand renewable energy are becoming visible across Asia, with Thailand, for example, pursuing the purchase of electricity from residential rooftop solar panels [47].

sections.title: 🌍 Expanding Global Climate Adaptation and Technological Cooperation
sections.content: Support for climate-vulnerable nations and international technological cooperation are crucial pillars of global climate response. Incheon City is playing a leading role by hosting the World Climate Technology Forum to apply Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology in climate-vulnerable nations [10, 11, 12]. The Delhi Declaration from the BRICS Summit suggests a shift in climate change priorities among Global South nations, calling for a multifaceted approach from the international community [71]. In the UK, applications for community climate change funds have opened, supporting grassroots climate action [65]. Research suggesting that microorganisms might hold the key to climate-resilient agriculture [70] demonstrates the potential of nature-based solutions. Furthermore, in Belgium, pine cone harvesting has been reported as a natural defense strategy against climate change [74]. With climate change threatening to permanently erase Bronze Age artifacts [73], the importance of cultural heritage preservation is also being highlighted.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing served as an opportunity to once again acknowledge the severity of the climate crisis, while also affirming the importance of practices, technological innovation, and international cooperation for carbon neutrality being pursued both domestically and internationally. This concludes today's climate briefing.
